correctness.rationale: Each strict successor stage removes a distinct original labelled arrow; if all stages below κ⁺ were strict this would inject κ⁺ into a set of at most κ arrows. First equality persists at successors and limits. Target restriction and intersections preserve transitivity and Euclideanness. In T_α each same-agent source belongs to at most one block, and X×Y with Y⊆X is K45. At stage ξ an arrow target of rank β≥ξ retains its parent-agent self-loop, and has an opposite-agent successor exactly if β>ξ. Thus precisely rank-ξ targets are removed; at a limit λ the retained ranks are exactly β≥λ. The root arrow to the rank-ξ child witnesses strictness for every ξ<α, and no arrows remain at α. For α=0 the lone world is edgeless; finite sequences have the asserted cardinal bound for each α<κ⁺, including finite α. In the one-agent argument every arrow target is reflexive by Euclideanness, and all its successors are also targets; the total relation on these serial target structures is an atom-free bisimulation. Hence all targets agree on a fixed atom-free formula, giving either no change or complete deletion. A depth-zero atom-free formula is model-independent.
residual_risks: Recorded rank-0 through rank-8 checks are finite; the limit and successor arguments above establish the unbounded assertion. No formal verification claimed.

value.rationale: The exact spectrum closes a construction-vs-cardinality gap in iterated belief change. A single minimal modal test, not a formula tuned to the ordinal, attains every allowable stage. This separates the expressive resources that support unbounded peeling from the one-agent and modality-free cases.
residual_risks: This is about whole-relation stabilization under target filtering on nonserial K45, not convergence of arbitrary truth values or the corresponding spectrum on S5 or KD45.
